name: cache-key
body:
The version/format/config identity that invalidates the whole scan cache when it drifts (`rust.apg.cache.manifest.CacheKey`): the binary's own version + the scanner JSONL schema/format + the ingestor projection-rules version + the scan config (languages, excludes, modules) + the classification-config identity of `apg/config.json`.

A mismatch forces a full load — for correctness rather than as a heuristic: the same content at the same commit assembled under a different config yields a different graph, so a cached projection produced under the old config is discarded. Equal inputs yield equal keys; any graph-affecting input drift moves the key. It is the value the shared fact store keys each per-file unit by (the store is repo-wide, shared across every worktree and branch of the repository), which is why a config change invalidates the whole store rather than one file.

The classification component is a stable digest of the parsed config's `default`, its ordered `types` rules (name, globs, names, and rule order), and its `structural` scope (include, exclude, code_type); it excludes the binary-managed `version` field and uses a distinct stable sentinel when the config is absent. Named by the code doc-comments in `rust.apg.cache` (module docs), `rust.apg.cache.manifest.CacheKey`, and `rust.apg.frontends`' `--cache-key` hand-off doc.
